chart.bar: largest strictly positive finite H1 lifetime; ties birth asc, death asc, index asc
chart.scale: midpoint (birth + death) / 2; edges with distance <= scale
chart.lift_solver: scipy.optimize.milp, zero objective, integrality all, threads 1, mip_rel_gap 0, presolve default
chart.gauge: fit_gauge(chart, m32[C*]) unchanged: s in (+1,-1) maximizing |mean(exp(i*s*phi) * conj(m32x + i*m32y))| over the C* landmarks; tie s=+1; phi <- (s*phi - arg(c)) mod 2pi; |c| finite and > 0; no other alignment threshold
chart.sigma: median(d8) over the charted landmarks C*: d8_i = 8th smallest distance from charted landmark i to the other charted landmarks (self excluded only)
chart.duplicate_rule: query with an exact zero distance: z = mean of exp(i*phi_j) over ALL landmarks at distance exactly 0; Invalid if 1 - |z| > 1e-8
chart.inherited_from: tools/c1prime/CONTRACT.json chart section at R_ref c460e24 (kernel keys, giant, val_support copied verbatim; equality checked by k4b_config.check_chart_equality); the frozen C1' CONTRACT is not edited
chart.landmarks: production: the 512 lowest-sequence_id rows of k4b cal b0 (3,072 rows), every sampled row; direct comparator: the 512 lowest-sequence_id rows of k4b val b0; step-0 control: the same 512 cal b0 landmarks; natural float64 resid_post_3/p32 activations; landmark_ids = 20-digit zero-padded sequence_id strings, ascending
chart.restriction: largest connected component C* of ({0..511}, edge_list(D, r)); ties to the component containing the smallest landmark index
chart.support_radius: 2 * quantile(d8, 0.99, method=inverted_cdf), d8 over D[np.ix_(C*, C*)]
chart.fidelity_domain: the direct chart's C*_val rows, in its landmark order, unmasked
chart.support_rule: C0-val: >= 507/512 supported (not every row); no fresh-test support gate (protocol 10)
chart.gate_rules: C0-cal: GIANT, lift, primitive, smoothing, gauge alignment finite > 0; C0-val: direct GIANT, support >= 507/512, fidelity >= 0.80, every bin >= 8, overall resultant <= 0.30; unmet -> INCONCLUSIVE/CHART_UNAVAILABLE

statements.aggregate_rule: any model FALSE -> FALSE; else every model TRUE (D2: TRUE or BY_CONSTRUCTION with >= 1 INFORMATIVE TRUE) -> TRUE; else NOT_EVALUABLE with reasons {reason: [models]}

error_statements.D1: false TRUE <= alpha per model (= stage C's SUPPORT level); false FALSE <= alpha per model
error_statements.D2: false FALSE <= alpha per model (Bonferroni over <= 11 pre-chart checkpoints at 1/720 each), <= 0.05 over three. TRUE rests on the absence of strong pre-chart evidence: the report states n_pre and max U^S + F+ before the onset
error_statements.D3: false TRUE <= 2 alpha (one false EXCLUDE at k_C or one false SUPPORT at 5000, intersection-union over models); false FALSE <= alpha per model per route
error_statements.D5: false early k_P <= alpha per model (Bonferroni via z_S); sigma at k_P <= alpha per side
error_statements.D6: false FALSE <= 2 alpha per model (one false strong bound on either side). TRUE means 'no certified loss', not 'monotone'

multiplicity: Per-checkpoint bands (ranks 84/4,917; central 95 % at 125/4,875) are nominal one-sided (1 - 0.05/3) percentile-bootstrap bounds conditional on the weights, the chart and the gauge; descriptive, with no family-wise claim over the 36 bands.
Anchored readings (sigma at k_C, k_L, k_P and at step 5000) are single pre-specified tests conditional on the anchor; no correction.

Existential readings (BEFORE, the D2 qualifier, D6 LOSS, the onset k_P) use the strong bounds at 1/720 per side: per-model family-wise level 12/720 = 1/60 per side, valid under the shared-row dependence; <= 0.05 per side over three models.
The strong bounds come from a separate 50,000-draw bootstrap (seed 620416, ranks 70/49,931); L^S > L or U^S < U can occur by Monte Carlo near the boundary and is listed as a diagnostic.
No correction across the six statements; they are descriptive summaries of one data set, partly nested (D2 and D3 share k_C), and must not be counted as independent confirmations.
The learning landmark (captured >= 0.8) is read on point estimates; its sampling error is reported (regret_se).

templates.D2_TRUE: In each model, no checkpoint before the first validated chart showed a chart phase certified above the margin (n_pre = {n_pre}; largest upper bound {max_upper}). The covariance was above the margin at the end. (qualifier per model: {qualifiers})
templates.D2_FALSE: In model {model}, at step {step} (before the first validated chart at step {chart_step}), a chart that had not passed validation already carried beyond-four covariance certified above 0.01 at the strong level.
templates.D3_TRUE: In each model, at the first checkpoint with a validated chart (steps {steps}), the covariance was certified below 0.01, and it was above 0.01 at step 5000: at this checkpoint resolution, the circle formed before it carried the beyond-four information.
templates.D3_CHART_AT_INIT: A model whose validated chart is already present at step 0 is NOT_EVALUABLE/CHART_AT_INIT, because a circle present in the untrained network does not count as formed during training.
templates.D3_FALSE: In model {model}, the first validated chart (step {step}) already carried it above 0.01.
templates.D4_TRUE: When captured first reached 0.8 (steps {steps}), the covariance was still certified below 0.01; it rose above 0.01 later. Captured 0.8 can be reached with last-four information alone in this world.
templates.D5_TRUE: When the predictions first beat every last-four predictor (steps {steps}), the chart phase already carried it.
templates.D5_FALSE: When the predictions first beat every last-four predictor (steps {steps}), the chart phase did not carry it.
templates.D6_TRUE: No model showed a certified loss after a certified gain; this does not mean monotone.

does_not_establish: 1 Use: no claim that the readout or the predictions use the beyond-four component of the chart phase, causally or otherwise (track U's question); D5 compares two onsets and is not a use test.
2 Training as a cause: checkpoints of one run are not independent experiments and there is no counterfactual.
3 Timing finer than the grid: timing is at the checkpoint grid 0, 50, 100, 200, 400, 700, 1000, 1500, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000 only; WITH means within the same grid interval.

4 Chart formation is measured by the stage-C gate rule on these rows; 'no chart' means the rule's gates failed, not that no circular structure exists; beyond-four information outside the chart phase is not measured.
5 Learning: captured >= 0.8 is a registered landmark, not a phase transition, and is reachable with last-four information; B2 is a normal-approximation lower bound.
6 Population: three runs of one recipe in one world; not the training-seed population; not other worlds, sites, positions, layers, harmonics or the y-coordinate.
7 Mechanism: no claim about how the circle or the history dependence is computed.
8 Simultaneity: the 36 bands are not simultaneous; curve shapes include shared-row noise; the six statements are not independent confirmations.
9 Unvalidated charts: their bounds are valid for that fixed field (Theorem A), but the field did not pass validation.
10 Step 0: an untrained network is a function of the whole history; covariance at step 0 is not learned.
11 Earlier verdicts: no new decision; stage C's SUPPORT, K4b's EXCLUSION and every earlier verdict stand; D1 is a replication on fresh rows with the same weights, not a fourth model.
12 D6: no certified loss is not monotone growth.
13 Licence conditions: all bounds are nominal percentile-bootstrap statements conditional on weights, charts and gauges; the documented-law transport assumes idealised sampler draws.
